title: Duel Decks: Zendikar vs. Eldrazi: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: Once a welcoming hub for explorers, Affa became a place of guarded tongues and quick defenses.
As the hedrons began to coalesce into colossal Eldrazi superstructures, the griffins were forced to seek new territory lest their aeries be crushed between the massive stone monoliths.
"'Invincible' is just a word." —Gideon Jura
A boon to those who cannot see in the dark. A bane to those who live in it.
"Petrifying gaze, deadly fangs, knifelike dorsal spines, venomous saliva . . . Am I missing anything? . . . Toxic bones? Seriously?" —Samila, Murasa Expeditionary House
"The elders say Zendikar has no safe, peaceful places. How would they know? They've never looked."
He'll cleave wood and bone alike to carve a path for his allies.
"Don't be fooled. If it were as docile as it looks, it would've died off long ago." —Yon Basrel, Oran-Rief survivalist
"This world will not be tamed."
The Roil redraws the world as it passes, leaving only the hedrons unchanged.
Adventuring bards recite *Chanter's Epics*, never-ending tales that keep their comrades' minds alert to danger.
Some druids nurture gardens. Others nurture continents.
"Survival rule 781: There are always more scute bugs." —Zurdi, goblin shortcutter
Its territory is defined by wherever it is at the moment.
"Life as we know it dangles on the brink of extinction. We must show the strength they would steal from us." —*The Invokers' Tales*
"The shadow travels toward the apex. I predict we will soon see the true measure of darkness."
"We suffer uneasy ground, unstable alliances, and unpredictable magic. Something you can truly trust is worth more than a chest of gold." —Nikou, Joraga bard
Every world is an organism, able to grow new lands. Some just do it faster than others.
The Eldrazi hunger without limit and consume without pause.
Your pleas for death shall go unheard.
"Whatever the Eldrazi's purpose is, it has nothing to do with something so insignificant as us." —Nirthu, lone missionary
"The brood lineages unfolded across the world, each patterned after one of three progenitors, each a study in mindless consumption." —*The Invokers' Tales*
Some humans willingly offered up their blood, hoping it would grant the vampire families the strength to stave off the Eldrazi.
His verdict is always guilty. His sentence is always death.
The mouth must be pried open before rigor mortis sets in. Otherwise the returning soul can find no ingress.
"Others ask why the Eldrazi destroy. I ask why they preserve." —Ganda, Goma Fada deserter
All the angel saw was her doom.
The dead know lessons the living haven't learned.
"Before I hire new recruits, I test how long they can hold their breath. You'd be surprised how often it comes up." —Zahr Gada, Halimar expedition leader
Wordlessly it leads its abhorrent brood.
"Play no favorites. Everybody dies." —Sparkmage saying
Just when you thought you'd be safe, in the middle of an open field with no Eldrazi around for miles.
"The purpose of existence is simple: everything is fuel for the magmaw." —Jaji, magmaw worshipper
Once thrown, twice burned.
"While we delay, they're on the move. They will not wait as we bicker. We are losing this war by moments as our goal slips beyond our reach." —Gideon Jura
What is mana but possibility, an idea not yet given form?
Scholars had puzzled for centuries over the ruins at Tal Terig. Its secrets had always lived within one rune-carved head.
Each temple is a door to a horrible future.
